source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: This took place on a Shabbat [Sabbath], when Yeshua was passing through sown fields. His disciples were picking the heads [of grain] and rubbing them in [their] hands and eating the kernels.

translation_notes: זה (consonants ז-ה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because the demonstrative 'this' fits the narrative introduction pointing to the event described.
כאשר (כ + אשר): The כ prefix + H834 'which/when' yields 'when/as', which fits the temporal clause introducing the scene.
ישוע: H3442 and H3443 are the same name Yeshua; chose H3442 as the primary entry for this proper name.
textual_notes: The word עשוי lacks Strong's candidates in the provided list. It appears to be a passive participle from עשה (to do/make), here functioning as 'it was done / it happened.' This is post-biblical Mishnaic Hebrew narrative style.
ב)בת appears to be בשבת (on Shabbat) with a scribal marker or damage obscuring the shin. The context of Sabbath controversy confirms this reading.
Several words (תלמידיו, לוקטין, ומוללין, ואוכלין, הגרעינים) are post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew forms not covered by Strong's biblical lexicon.

verses.literal: It-happened this on-Shabbat when Yeshua [was] passing through-fields sown his-disciples [were] picking the-ears and-rubbing them with-hands and-eating the-kernels

verses.translation: And some of those Pharisees [Perushim] were saying to them, 'Why are you doing what is not fitting [or: proper, permitted] to do on the Shabbat [Sabbath]?'

translation_notes: ומקצת: H7117/H7118 both mean 'a portion/end'. With the prefix ו (and) + מ (from), this yields 'and some of', which fits the partitive sense here.
להם: The preposition ל + הם H1992 'them' = 'to them'. H3859 'to rankle' makes no contextual sense in a dialogue introduction.
למה: ל + מה H4100 'what' = 'for what' i.e. 'why', standard interrogative usage.

עשות: The provided candidates H6219 'shining/polished' and H6220 'Ashvath' do not fit. This is clearly the infinitive construct of עשה (to do/make), a standard biblical form not needing a separate Strong's entry from the root.
textual_notes: אתם is listed only as H864 'Etham, a place', but in context this is clearly the second person plural pronoun 'you' (אַתֶּם), a common word that may not have matched the consonantal lookup properly.
ב)בת again appears to be בשבת with scribal damage or notation obscuring the shin.

verses.literal: And-some of-those Pharisees saying to-them why you doing what [that] is-not fitting to-do on-Shabbat

verses.translation: And Yeshua answered and said to them, 'Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him? [No one sews] from your [own garments] — [one who] joins the new tears [or: breaks away] the old.'

translation_notes: ענה: Candidates include H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6034 'Anah (name)'. Chose H6030 because the pattern 'answered and said' is a standard dialogue formula.
ואמר: H559 'to say' fits the narrative formula perfectly. H563 'a lamb' and H564 'Immer (name)' produce incoherent images here.
דוד: H1732 'David' fits as the historical figure being referenced. H1730 'uncle/lover' and H1731 'pot/basket' do not fit the narrative about reading Scripture.
כשהיה: כש + היה H1961 'when it was/existed' — temporal clause 'when there was'. H1962 'ruin' does not fit.
רעב: H7456 'to hunger', H7457 'hungry', H7458 'hunger (noun)'. With לו ('to him'), the noun H7458 'hunger' fits: 'when hunger was to him' = 'when he was hungry'.
הוא: H1931 'he' as emphatic pronoun fits the appositive construction 'he and those with him'.
החדש: H2319 'new' fits as an adjective describing a patch or garment. H2320 'new moon/month' is possible but less coherent with the tearing/breaking imagery.
משבר: H7665 'to burst/break' as a participle 'breaking' fits the image of new fabric tearing away from old. H4866 'womb opening' and H4867 'sea-breaker' do not fit.
הישן: H3465 'old' fits perfectly as 'the old [garment]'. H3462 'to sleep' and H3463 'sleepy' produce incoherent images.
textual_notes: The final clause 'משללכם יחבר החדש משבר הישן' appears to be a separate saying about patching garments — joining new to old causes tearing. The word משללכם is puzzling: it could be מ + שלל + כם 'from your spoils/garments' (שלל can mean 'plunder' or 'stripped garments'). This clause seems to be a parable about not mixing new and old, which may be contextually displaced or part of a composite teaching.
The transition from the David narrative to the garment saying is abrupt, suggesting either a textual compression or a different verse division than expected.

verses.literal: And-Yeshua answered and-said to-them not have-you-read what did David when-was to-him hunger he and-those who-were with-him from-your-spoils he-joins the-new breaking the-old

verses.translation: When he entered the house of God and took the bread of the Presence [literally: bread of the face] and ate [it] and gave [it] to those who were with him — and it is not fitting [or: permitted] for any person to eat it, only the priests.

translation_notes: לבית: H1004 'house' with preposition ל 'to' = 'to the house of'. H1006 'Bajith (place)' does not fit the narrative about entering God's dwelling.
האל: H410 'God/mighty one' with the article ה = 'the God'. H408/H413 (negation/preposition) make no sense after 'house of'. This is 'the house of God'.
ולקח: H3947 'to take' fits perfectly — David took the bread. H3948 'instruction' does not fit as a verb here.
לחם: H3899 'bread/food' fits as the object of 'took'. H3898 'to battle' and H3901 'battle' produce incoherent images with 'the face/presence'.
שהוא: H1931 'he' as the relative clause subject 'that he [was]' fits. The שׁ prefix is the Mishnaic relative pronoun.
ואין: H369 'non-entity / not' = 'there is not / it is not', fitting the prohibition statement. H370/H371 do not fit.
לשום: H7760 'to put/set' is possible but here לשום functions as 'for any' (ל + שום in post-biblical Hebrew = 'for any'). H7762 'garlic' is absurd in context.
אדם: H120 'human being/person' fits perfectly. H121 'Adam (name)', H123 'Edom' do not fit the generic usage here.
רק: H7535 'only/merely' fits the restrictive clause. H7534 'emaciated' and H7536 'spittle' are contextually impossible.
textual_notes: הכה!נים appears to have a scribal mark (!) within the word, likely הכהנים 'the priests' with some notation or damage at the he/nun junction.

verses.literal: When-he-entered to-house-of the-God and-took bread the-face and-ate and-gave to-whoever that-he [was] with-him and-not fitting for-any person to-eat-it only the-priests

verses.translation: And [I] say to you: how [great] a master [or: lord, sovereign] he is — the Son of Man — and also of the Shabbat [Sabbath].

translation_notes: אדון: H113 'sovereign/controller/lord' fits perfectly — declaring authority. H114 'Addon (name)' does not fit a declarative statement about lordship.
הוא: H1931 'he' as emphatic pronoun in a nominal clause 'he is'. H1933/H1934 'to exist' would be redundant with the copular function.
בן: H1121 'a son' in construct with האדם = 'son of the man/human'. H1122 'Ben (name)' does not fit this title.
האדם: H120 'human being' with article = 'the man/the human'. This is the title 'Son of Man'. H121 'Adam' or H123 'Edom' are less fitting for the title.
ועוד: H5750 'again/also/furthermore' fits as an additive — 'and also [lord] of the Shabbat'. H5749 'to testify' does not fit syntactically.
מה: H4100 'what/how' — here functioning as an exclamatory 'how [great] a lord he is'.
textual_notes: מה&בת appears to be מהשבת 'of the Shabbat' with the & symbol marking a scribal issue at the shin. Combined with ועוד, the meaning is 'and also of the Shabbat' — i.e., the Son of Man is lord also of the Sabbath.
ואומר: The Strong's candidate H201 'Omar (grandson of Esau)' is clearly wrong for this context. This is a participial form of אמר (to say) = 'and saying / and I say'.
The syntax 'מה אדון הוא' could be parsed either as exclamatory ('what a lord he is!') or interrogative ('what lord is he?'). The exclamatory reading fits a proclamation of authority better.

verses.literal: And-saying to-you what master he [is] son-of the-man and-also-of [the]-Shabbat

verses.translation: And it happened on yet another Shabbat [Sabbath] that he entered the synagogue [house of assembly] and was teaching. And there was a certain person there who had a withered [or: dried-up] hand.
words: and it happened / and it was done

translation_notes: היה: H1961 'to exist/become/come to pass' fits the narrative frame. H1962 'ruin' does not fit.
עוד: H5750 'again/yet/another' — indicating another Sabbath occasion. H5749 'to testify' does not fit.
בבית: ב + H1004 'house' = 'in the house of'. The construct with הכנסת gives 'house of assembly' = synagogue.
ומלמד: H3925 'to teach/goad to learn' as a participle 'and teaching' fits the scene. H4451 'a goad for oxen' is the noun form — less fitting since the context requires a verbal participle.
והיה: H1961 'and it was / and there was' continues the narrative.
שם: H8033 'there' fits the locative sense. H8034 'name' does not fit 'and there was ___ a person'.
אדם: H120 'human being/person' fits. Used generically for 'a certain man'.
אחד: H259 'one/a certain' fits as an indefinite article equivalent. H258 'to unify/collect thoughts' does not fit as an adjective here.
שהיה: ש (relative) + H1961 'was' = 'who was / that had'.
יד: H3027 'hand' fits the body part being described. H3028 is the Aramaic equivalent.
יבשה: H3004 'dry ground' — the same consonants serve as the feminine adjective 'dry/withered' describing the hand.
textual_notes: ונע!שה has a scribal mark (!) that likely indicates ונעשה 'and it was done / and it happened', a niphal form of עשה.
מ&בת again has the & marker, likely representing משבת / שבת 'Shabbat'.
יבשה (H3004) is listed as 'dry ground' but the same consonants form the feminine adjective 'dry/withered' modifying יד (hand). The adjectival reading is required by context.

verses.literal: And-it-happened [it] was yet [another] Shabbat one that-he-entered in-house-of the-assembly and-teaching and-was there [a] person one that-was to-him [a] hand withered

verses.translation: And the scribes [Soferim] and the Pharisees [Perushim] were watching [closely] whether he would heal him on the Shabbat [Sabbath], so that they might find grounds [or: occasion, basis] to accuse him.
words: that they would accuse him / inform against him

translation_notes: אם: H518 'whether/if' fits the indirect question of whether he would heal. H517 'mother' is contextually impossible.
מקום: H4725 'a standing/place/spot' here used figuratively as 'grounds/basis/occasion' for accusation. H6965 'to rise' is the verbal root and does not fit the noun needed here.
textual_notes: שילשינוהו is a post-biblical Hebrew form meaning 'that they would inform against him / accuse him / denounce him' (from the root לשן, related to לשון 'tongue', i.e., to use the tongue against someone). Not in Strong's biblical lexicon.
בע!בור has a scribal mark, likely בעבור 'for the sake of / in order that'.
ב&בת again = בשבת 'on the Shabbat'.

verses.literal: And-watching the-scribes and-the-Pharisees if he-will-heal-him on-Shabbat in-order-that they-would-find [a] place that-they-would-accuse-him

verses.translation: And Yeshua said to the man whose hand was withered, 'Rise and stand in the middle.' And he rose and stood on his feet.

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say' is the clear choice for the dialogue verb. H563 'lamb' and H564 'Immer' are contextually impossible.
לאיש: H376 'a man/individual' with preposition ל = 'to the man'. H377 'to act manly' does not fit a prepositional target.
שידו: Listed candidate H3035 'Jiddo (name)' does not apply. This is ש (relative) + יד (hand) + ו (his) = 'whose hand / that his hand'. The consonants ידו here are יד + pronominal suffix.
קום: H6965 'to rise' as imperative 'rise!' fits the command. H6966 is the Aramaic equivalent.
ועמד: H5975 'to stand' fits perfectly as the narrative completion of the command. H5976 'to shake', H5977 'a fixed spot', H5978 'along with' do not fit.
על: H5921 'upon/on' fits 'stood on his feet'. H5923 'a yoke' is contextually impossible.
textual_notes: וע!מוד has a scribal mark, likely ועמוד 'and stand' — imperative of עמד.
יבשה again functions as the feminine adjective 'withered/dry' rather than H3004's nominal gloss 'dry ground'.

verses.literal: And-Yeshua said to-the-man that-his-hand [was] withered rise and-stand in-the-middle and-he-rose and-stood on his-feet

verses.translation: And Yeshua said to them, 'I ask you: is it fitting [or: permitted, proper] to do good or to do evil on the Shabbat [Sabbath]? [Is it fitting] to save a life [or: soul, being] or to destroy [it]?'
words: the soul / the life / the being

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say' — dialogue introduction, as before.
להם: ל + הם H1992 'them' = 'to them'.
אם: H518 'whether/if' introduces the question. H517 'mother' does not fit.
טוב: H2896 'good (adjective)' fits as the object-concept of doing. H2895 'to do good (verb)' is possible but the infinitive ע!שות already provides the verbal element, so the adjective/noun is needed.
רע: H7451 'bad/evil' fits as the contrasting pair with 'good'. H7452 'crash/noise', H7453 'associate/friend', H7454 'thought' do not fit the moral contrast.
הנפש: H5315 'a breathing creature / soul / life' fits the question about saving life. H5314 'to breathe/be refreshed' is the verb form and does not fit with the article ה.
textual_notes: א!ני has a scribal mark, likely אני 'I'.
ע!שות has scribal marks, likely עשות 'to do' — infinitive construct of עשה.
ב&בת again = בשבת 'on the Shabbat'.

שואל: The provided consonantal candidates only list אל forms (H408–H413), but this is clearly שׁ-ו-א-ל from the root שאל 'to ask/inquire' (H7592), in participial form 'asking'. The shin was apparently not parsed in the candidate list.

verses.literal: And-Yeshua said to-them I asking you whether fitting to-do good or to-do evil on-Shabbat or the-soul to-save or to-destroy

verses.translation: And when he looked at all of them, he said to the man, 'Stretch out [or: send forth] your hand.' And the man stretched out his hand, and immediately it was healed [or: restored].
words: and immediately / and from the hand
it was healed / it was restored

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say' for the dialogue verb, as consistently throughout.
לאיש: H376 'a man' with ל = 'to the man'. Same as section 8.

שלח (first): H7971 'to send away/out' = 'stretch out / extend'. This is the imperative command. H7973 'spear/branch', H7974 'Shelach (name)', H7975 'Shiloach (fountain)' do not fit a command to extend one's hand. H3892 'fresh/unused' (from לח) does not fit either.
שלח (second): Same as above, H7971 in completed action — 'he stretched out'.
והאיש: H376 'the man' with conjunctive ו and article ה.
ידו: H3035 'Jiddo (name)' is the only listed candidate, but this is clearly יד 'hand' (H3027) + ו (his) = 'his hand'. The pronominal suffix created a consonantal match with the name.

ומיד: ו + מ + יד. H3027 'hand' forms the basis, but ומיד in post-biblical Hebrew is an adverb meaning 'immediately / at once' (literally 'from the hand' = 'on the spot'). Both the literal and idiomatic meanings work.
textual_notes: וכא!שר has a scribal mark, likely וכאשר 'and when/as'.

ומיד is ambiguous between the literal 'and from [his] hand' and the post-biblical adverbial usage 'immediately'. The adverbial reading is more natural: the healing happened instantly upon stretching out the hand.
נתרפאה is a hitpael/nitpael form of רפא 'to heal' — 'it was healed / it healed itself', with feminine agreement matching יד 'hand' (feminine in Hebrew).

verses.literal: And-when he-looked [at] all-of-them he-said to-the-man stretch-out your-hand and-the-man stretched-out his-hand and-immediately it-was-healed

verses.translation: And they were filled with rage [or: wrath, fury], speaking among themselves: What shall we do about Yeshua [Joshua/Jesus] — when he entered, as when he entered

translation_notes: מלאים (מלא + ים): The root מלא means 'full/filled'; the ים suffix here functions as a plural adjective — 'filled.' The candidate H366 אים 'frightful' shares only the suffix. The context of rage/fury fits 'filled with fury' perfectly.
מה: Candidates H4100 and H4101 are essentially the same interrogative 'what?' — fits the context of deliberation: 'what shall we do?'
מישוע (מ + ישוע): The prefix מ means 'from/about'; ישוע is the proper name Yeshua (H3442/H3443). Context of discussing what to do 'about Yeshua' is coherent.
textual_notes: The text appears to have a scribal repetition or dittography: 'כשנכנס כ שנכנס' — 'when he entered as when he entered.' This may be a copying error, or it may be an emphatic construction. The nw in נע!שה appears to have a scribal mark (!) which may indicate damage or uncertainty in the manuscript.

verses.literal: And them filled [with] fury speaking among themselves what shall we do about Yeshua when he entered as when he entered

verses.translation: And it came to pass in those days that Yeshua ascended upon a certain [or: one] mountain and [was] praying, and in the prayer of God [the Mighty One] he was awake [or: watchful, vigilant]

translation_notes: ההם: H1992 'they/those' — as a demonstrative adjective modifying 'the days,' yielding 'those days.' H1990 'Ham' (a place) and H1991 'abundance' do not fit.

עלה: H5927 'to ascend' produces a coherent image of going up a mountain. H5928/H5930 'holocaust/offering' would be a noun and doesn't fit the narrative verb slot. H5929 'leaf/foliage' is nonsensical here.
בהר: H2022 'a mountain' — with prefix ב 'on/in.' H2023 'Hor' is a specific peak; context says 'one mountain' generically, so H2022 is better.
אחד: H259 'one/a certain' — fits 'a certain mountain.' H258 'to unify/collect thoughts' is a verb and doesn't fit the adjective slot.

האל: H410 'God/the Mighty One' — with the definite article ה, 'the God.' In context of 'prayer of God,' this is the most coherent. H408/409 'not' makes no sense. H411 'these/those' would be odd after 'prayer of.'
היה: H1961 'to be/was' — standard narrative verb. H1962 'ruin' is a noun and doesn't fit.

ער: H6145 'a foe (as watchful)' — but the root ער fundamentally means 'watchful/awake.' In context of all-night prayer, 'he was awake/vigilant' is the natural reading. H6144 'Ar' (a place) and H6147 'Er' (a name) produce nonsense in this sentence.
textual_notes: ער could be read as 'awake/watchful' (from the root meaning wakefulness underlying H6145) or as the proper noun Er (H6147). The narrative context of prayer through the night strongly favors 'awake/watchful.' The word ונעשה at the beginning could also be parsed as 'and we shall do' (1cp imperfect of עשה), but contextually 'and it came to pass' fits the narrative frame better.

verses.literal: And it came to pass in the days those that Yeshua ascended on a mountain one and praying and in the prayer of God he was awake

verses.translation: And when it was morning, he called [or: summoned] his disciples and selected [or: chose] twelve from those whom he called sent-ones [emissaries, apostles]

translation_notes: וכאשר: ו + כ + אשר — H834 'who/which/when' with כ 'as/when' and ו 'and' — yields 'and when.' H833 'to be happy,' H835 'happiness,' H836 'Asher,' H838 'a step' — none fit the temporal conjunction needed here.
היה: H1961 'was/came to be' — with בקר following, 'it was morning.' H1962 'ruin' is nonsensical.
בקר: H1242 'morning/dawn' — 'it was morning' is the most natural continuation. H1241 'cattle' would produce 'it was cattle,' which is bizarre. H1239 'to inspect' doesn't fit after היה.
קרא: H7121 'to call/summon' — the standard meaning for summoning disciples. H7122 'to encounter' is possible but less specific. H7124 'partridge' is a noun and doesn't fit.
ובחר: H977 'to select/choose' — perfect fit for choosing disciples. H2715 'noble/pure' is an adjective and doesn't parse as a verb here.
עשר: H6235 'ten' — combined with שנים 'two' yields 'twelve.' H6238 'to grow rich' and H6239 'wealth' produce nonsense.
שקרא: ש + קרא — H7121 'whom he called' — relative pronoun + verb, naming them as sent-ones.
textual_notes: שלוחים is not in the provided Strong's candidates — it is derived from the root שלח (to send), meaning 'sent-ones/emissaries.' This is the Hebrew equivalent of the concept of apostles.

verses.literal: And when it was morning he called to his disciples and chose two ten from those whom he called sent-ones

verses.translation: Shimon [Simon], whom he called Kepha [Cephas/Rock], and Andrei [Andrew] his brother, Yaaqov [Jacob/James], Yochanan [John], Philip, Bartholomew

translation_notes: שמעון: H8095 'Shimon' — the proper name, one of Jacob's sons. The other candidates (H4583 'abode,' H5771 'perversity') are component roots but the full form שמעון is clearly the personal name in this list of disciples.
שקרא: H7121 'whom he called' — relative ש + קרא 'called.' Same usage as in the previous section. He gave Shimon the name Kepha.

אחיו: H283 'Achio' is listed as a proper name, but in context this is אח + יו 'his brother' — Andrei is identified as Shimon's brother. The possessive suffix makes this a common noun, not the proper name Achio.
textual_notes: אחיו could technically be the proper name Achio (H283), but in context — immediately following Andrei and preceding a list of other names — it clearly means 'his brother,' identifying Andrei as Shimon's brother. כיפא, ואנדרי, פיליף, and ברתלמי are transliterated foreign/Aramaic names without Strong's numbers.

verses.literal: Shimon whom he called Kepha and Andri his brother Yaaqov Yochanan Pilip Bartalmay

verses.translation: Mattityah [Matthew/Gift of Yah], Toma [Thomas], Yaaqov [Jacob/James] [son of] Chalphi [Alphaeus], and Shimon who is called [the Zealot]

translation_notes: ושמעון: H8095 'Shimon' with prefix ו 'and.' H4583/H4584 'abode/Maon' are component roots but the full form is clearly the personal name in this name list.
textual_notes: The word ]קני[ appears in brackets in the source text, suggesting manuscript damage or editorial uncertainty. It likely represents קנאי 'zealot/zealous one' from the root קנא (to be zealous). חלפי appears to be a patronymic (Aramaic/Hebrew form of Alphaeus) identifying which Yaaqov this is.

verses.literal: Mattityah Toma Yaaqov Chalphi and Shimon who is called [Zealot]

verses.translation: Yehudah [Judah/Jude], [and] Yehudah [Judah] man of Qeriyot [Kerioth/Iscariot], who was a betrayer [traitor]

translation_notes: איש: H376 'a man' — in construct with קריות produces 'man of Qeriyot,' the Hebrew equivalent of 'Iscariot.' H377 'to act manly' is a verb and doesn't fit the nominal slot.
שהיה: ש + היה — H1961 'who was/existed.' H1962 'ruin' or H3050 'Yah' do not fit this relative clause construction.

בוגד: The root בגד means 'to deal treacherously/betray.' The candidates listed under גד (H1407-H1410) are for the sub-root only. The full form בוגד is a participial form of בגד (Strong's H898), meaning 'betrayer/traitor.'
textual_notes: The two occurrences of יהודה likely refer to two different persons: the first is Judah (Jude, son of James or Thaddaeus) and the second is Judah of Qeriyot (Judas Iscariot). The text lists them sequentially without a conjunction between them, which is slightly unusual but the identifying phrase 'man of Qeriyot' disambiguates.

verses.literal: Yehudah Yehudah man of Qeriyot who was a betrayer

verses.translation: And he descended from the mountain with them and stood in a level [or: flat, open] place, with a company [gathering] of his disciples and a great multitude of people from all of Yehudah [Judea] and Yerushalem [Jerusalem] and from beyond the sea [or: across the coast], and Tsor [Tyre] and Tsidon [Sidon]

translation_notes: וירד: H3381 'to descend' — he came down from the mountain. H3382 'Jered' is a proper name and doesn't fit the verb slot with ו-consecutive.

ההר: H2022 'mountain' with definite article — 'the mountain' previously mentioned. H2023 'Hor' is a specific named peak; the definite article pointing back to the previously mentioned mountain favors H2022.
ועמד: H5975 'to stand' — 'and he stood.' This is the most natural reading. H5976 'to shake' produces an odd image. H5977 'a spot' is a noun. H5978 'along with' is a preposition.
במקום: H4725 'a standing place/location' with prefix ב — 'in a place.' H6965 'to rise' is a verb root that doesn't fit the nominal construction here.

חרב: H2720 'parched/dry/level' — describing the terrain of the place. In context of descending from a mountain to stand on flat ground, 'level/flat' (a dry plain as opposed to a mountainous area) makes the most sense. H2719 'sword' would produce 'a place of sword' — possible but forced. H2722 'Choreb/Horeb' would mean he stood at Mount Sinai, which contradicts just descending from a different mountain. H2717 'to desolate' is a verb.
עם: H5971 'a people/nation' — 'a multitude of people.' H5973 'with' is a preposition and doesn't fit after רוב 'multitude of.'
מכל: מ + כל — H3605 'all/every' with prefix מ 'from' — 'from all of.'

translation_notes: והוא: H1931 'he' — emphatic pronoun 'and he.' H1933/H1934 'to be/exist' are verbs that don't fit with the following participle as naturally.

verses.literal: Like he is to a man who builds [a] house who deep sets back the foundation upon the stone and when there was [a] great flood of water the torrent came upon that house and was not able to shake it for it was founded upon the stone

verses.translation: But whoever hears my words and does not put them into practice [or: action] — he is comparable to a person building a house upon the ground without a foundation. And the water from the torrent came and struck it, and immediately it fell, and the ruin [or: destruction, devastation] of that house was great.

translation_notes: דומה: Candidates: H1745 'silence/death', H1746 'Dumah (place)'. As in section 6, this is clearly from דמה 'to resemble.' 'He is like/comparable' fits; 'he is silence/death' does not.
הוא: H1931 'he.' Pronoun subject of the comparison.
לאדם: Chose H120 'human being' for the same reasons as section 7.
בונה: Candidates: H946 'Bunah (name)', H5089 'lamentation.' Neither fits. This is the Qal active participle of בנה 'to build' — 'building.'
בית (both): H1004 'house' — same reasoning as section 7.
על: H5921 'upon' — building upon the ground.

בלא: Candidates: H1080 'to afflict', or ב + לא H3808 'without.' Chose ב + לא because 'without a foundation' produces the coherent contrast with the previous house built on rock. 'To afflict a foundation' is incoherent.
המים: Candidates: H4325 'water', H3220-H3222 (sea/spring). Chose H4325 'the water' as it matches the torrent/flood imagery.
מנחל: Candidates: H5157 'to inherit', H5158 'torrent/stream.' Chose H5158 because 'from the torrent' parallels section 7's הנחל.
ומיד: The candidate יד H3027 means 'hand,' and מיד literally means 'from hand' but idiomatically means 'immediately/at once.' This is the standard Hebrew idiom for immediacy.
נפל: Candidates: H5307 'to fall', H5308 (Aramaic), H5309 'abortion/something fallen.' Chose H5307 because 'it fell' describes the house collapsing — the natural image.
גדול: H1419 'great.' Unambiguous in context — 'great ruin.'
textual_notes: בלא: Could be read as H1080 'to afflict' or as the preposition ב + negation לא 'without.' The latter is overwhelmingly more natural: 'a house upon the ground without a foundation.'
דומה: Same candidate-list gap as sections 6-7. The root דמה 'to resemble' is not listed but is clearly intended.

ומיד: Literally 'and from hand' but idiomatically 'immediately.' The concrete meaning 'from the hand/power [of the flood]' is also plausible, though the idiomatic reading fits better with the rapid sequence of events described.
